analysis:
CHANGELOG.md (units 7e16eb3337db8652:12 and :13) is documentation only. It has no executable effect. Its descriptions of the profiler, runtime manifest and release behavior match the existing T-051 and attestation material, and it introduces no new trust assumptions.

LaunchAgent.swift has two changes (units 72a619a12f7f3e12:0, :1 and :2).

1. plistPath() and logPath() (lines ~21 and ~28) now resolve the home directory through LaunchctlControl.homeDirectory() instead of FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser. The LaunchctlControl source was not supplied. If that helper derives the path from an environment variable such as HOME or SUDO_USER rather than the passwd entry, the LaunchAgent plist location could shift. That would affect TB-003 (operator vs process) and the provider launch and update path, so it needs a follow-up check. The operator already controls the machine under the threat model, so the impact looks low and is not provable from the visible code.

2. restartAfterDrain() (lines ~166-186) now polls isLoaded() for up to 60s at 0.25s intervals before calling loadService(). It is an availability and race fix. It changes no trust or authorization state. The disableAutomaticStartup fence and loadService's re-enable logic are unchanged. If the job is still loaded after the timeout, bootstrap may fail and throw. That is an operational failure, not a security regression.

No findings against T-041, TB-007 or the other indexed threats. Reviewers of the next pass should read LaunchctlControl.homeDirectory() and confirm that it matches the passwd-based home directory semantics.
